doc.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021

title: Subbing for Gil Evans and Sting rehearsal
summary: He tells how Gil Evans phoned him to sub on baritone and bass clarinet at a rehearsal with Sting, paid $40, and names Evans a major influence.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: One of my favorite writers. I had one experience with him by the way, about a year before he died. This was the summer of ’87. It was a Monday morning and I was just lying in bed. The phone rings and I hear this voice at the other end of the phone, “This is Gil Evans,” who I’d never met before. He said, “Maria Schneider gave me your number. I’m doing a rehearsal this afternoon and I need a sub for Howard Johnson on baritone and bass clarinet. Can you do it? I’ll pay you.” And I resisted the temptation to say, “No, it’s okay I’ll pay you.” So I grabbed my baritone and bass clarinet and I go downtown to the west 20s and I walked into this studio and guys are just standing around warming up, whatever. And I look around and I see this tall, good looking guy who looked vaguely familiar. And I looked at him for about a minute and I realized this was Sting. And what © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

this was, this was a rehearsal of Gil’s band plus Sting as a guest soloist, they were going to go to the Umbria Jazz Festival. So what we rehearsed was — Maria and Tom Malone had written some charts on Police tunes like “Synchronicity” and “Roxanne.” And they had a few charts in Gil’s book from that Jimi Hendrix album that he had done in the 70s. Those charts were not written by Gil by the way, they were by somebody else. And they were really not much, frankly. That album is not one of Gil’s great records. But anyway so I did the rehearsal and he gave me 40 bucks, two 20 dollar bills. I should have kept them but I didn’t I spent them like an idiot. But that was my one experience with Gil. And Sting was great, he was a sweet guy and totally there for the music, no ego, no rock star pretentions, he was just one of the guys, he was there for the music. So it was a nice little experience.
Nice. I don’t think I would have —

Aside from that I mean Gil is one of my big influences as a writer and I know I’m far from alone in that respect. But I mean from the time when — I was still in high school when I first heard “Miles Ahead” and from then on I became a huge Gil Evans fan.
